name: Fitness Story NW
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the
transcription, the rewrite, the block at the foot of the frame and
every number in it are the same and are named here rather than
restated. What makes this show itself is one sentence long - it is set
in Century Gothic Bold, on a card, in a cream, a black and a navy the
user pairs per frame, with picked words told apart by colour alone -
and everything below is that sentence.
The NW in the name is the account's, the way the DE is in Fitness
Story DE and the NW in Crowned Ladies NW: it says which of the brand's
feeds this is and not what language the app is in. What lands on the
frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying, put through
the transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every channel here;
nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app itself says
is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
It shares a brand with Fitness Story and Fitness Story DE, and since
it took the card back it shares their shape as well: a coloured slab
at the foot of the frame and a palette handed to the user for the
type and for the slab. What it still does not share is the picked
word that changes CUT - there is one cut of Century Gothic here, so a
picked word changes colour instead (see below).
Written as its own folder rather than as an override of its siblings,
for the reason content/README.md gives: a channel is a folder that
gets dropped in. The prose below therefore points at hall-of-femme and
at crowned-ladies-fr wherever the reasoning is the same, and states
its own only where this pack actually decides something.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report.
Stated as a reference and not as numbers, because this channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not - and a pack
that restates a shared answer is a pack that can be missing a piece of
it. That is not hypothetical: channels arrived under this heading
captioning their frames with the transcript as spoken, because the
folder they were copied from predated `rewrite`.

_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Century Gothic Bold, in a cream, a black or a navy the user pairs
per frame, on a card, in one cut throughout.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform text box, where the block stands on the frame, the drag, the
shape of the card, the word highlight - is the Snapchat caption design
and is stated once, in content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This
pack states what makes it this show.
Century Gothic is a geometric sans built on circles - Monotype's
answer to ITC Avant Garde - and the Bold was chosen as the weight that
could stand on a photograph without a card: a 400-weight geometric
has thin joins where the circles meet the stems, and at 700 the stems
are even and heavy the whole way round.
It used to stand on the photograph on the strength of that, in the
cream alone, with a dark drop shadow. The show has since asked for
colours for the letters AND for a ground behind them, which is a
request for a card - the panel palette cannot exist without one (see
editor.paletteOf). So it is on the card its two Fitness Story siblings
already use, and what follows from that is written once, in
content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its caption on the
photograph may take the card back'.
It is also WIDE, which is the one thing to know before writing for it
and is measured in content/faces/century-gothic-bold.json rather than
here: twenty capitals can run past the 486px a line has, so the
occasional round sentence breaks at nineteen characters instead of the
preset's twenty. The wrapper does that on its own and nobody sees it
(see the two ceilings in js/caption.js) - it is noted because a caption
here takes a line more often than the same sentence on a narrower
sibling, and four lines is what the block is written to.
Uppercased, inherited, for the reason every one of its neighbours is:
at 40px with twenty characters to a line the caption is three short
beats rather than a paragraph, and capitals are what those are set in.
It costs nothing here - a geometric sans is a face whose capitals are
the circles and the straight lines it was drawn from, and this one's
round O and pointed A are what it is recognised by.

_comment_color: The cream, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is set
in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no colour
of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor). It
opens the list in `colors` below, so the cream swatch is the one
shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
#FEEECA is a warm off-white and not a white, and that stays the
brand. Its relative luminance is about 0.86, so it stands 18 times
clear of a black and barely clear of a white - which is why the
card this show opens on is the black one (see `panel` below).
_comment_colors: The show's cream, then the black and the navy it asked for,
offered for the letters and for the card behind them - three
buttons each in the title panel (see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same three in both lists and in one order, which is what
Fitness Story and Fitness Story DE do and for their reason: the
point is the PAIRING. Cream on black is what the show opens on;
cream on navy is a button away. Black on navy is a pairing the
list allows and nobody will keep - the user can see the caption
has sunk and presses another swatch.
No `colors.highlight`, and the row is there all the same: a pack
that names none offers the picked words this same list (see
_comment_highlight: The preset's word highlight, set in the block's own face and its
own cream. Picked words are told apart by COLOUR, and the colour is
the user's, from the highlight row every palette now carries.
This show used to have none, and of the three things a highlight
could be, colour was ruled out because it would split a colour
inside one sentence that the user, not the pack, was meant to
choose. The highlight row answers that: the split is now the
user's choice too. Until that row is pressed on a frame, a picked
word looks exactly like its neighbours and follows the letters'
colour, so nothing changes for anybody who never reaches for it.
Written down once, for all nine packs that made this change, in
content/README.md under 'Every palette offers the picked words
too'.
The other two are still out, for the reasons they always were: the
app carries one cut of Century Gothic and a synthesised weight is
measured as well as drawn, and a box on a card is a second shape
inside the first. The `color` is stated rather than inherited
because the skeleton's is white, and a highlight that starts in a
colour the block is not would be the pack choosing the split after
all.
_comment_panel: Black, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
Black because it is the first colour the show asked for and the
cream stands 18 times clear of it (see `color` above) - the dark
edge the old drop shadow gave each letter, given to the whole line
instead. The navy card is a button away.
